audit_notes: Model: soiling kinetics of the exposed sheet over one renewal cycle in normalized age s = t/T (first-order saturating soiling written as a second-order linear BVP: a(0)=0 fresh sheet, Robin at s=1 restating da/dt = (a_sat - a)/tau). Closed form a(s) = a_sat*(1 - exp(-T*s/tau)); the metric is the cycle-mean absorptance increase, transformed into the daily-mean roof heat flux with the same sol-air/U model as the other roof concepts. Checks: tau = 1 year and a_sat = 0.20 are consistent with CRRC-type ageing (most loss in year 1). Design T = 2 years: mean a = 0.2*(1 - 0.5*(1 - e^-2)) = 0.114 -> mean SR 0.81. Baseline: acrylic cool coat repainted every 10 years (T = 3.2e8 s), a_sat 0.18, SR 0.85: mean a = 0.18*(1 - 0.1*(1 - e^-10)) = 0.162 -> mean SR 0.69, eps 0.90. Hand result: design q = 0.5*(0.194*300 + 150 - 0.92*85)/15.5 = 4.19 W/m2, baseline 0.5*(0.312*300 + 150 - 76.5)/15.5 = 5.39 W/m2, gain ~22 %. Important caveats: (1) the renewal period is an input; the thermal-fatigue pacing that should produce it is not modelled, and interlayer fatigue lives scatter by a factor of 3-10, so the design could shed after months or never; (2) the gain is quite sensitive to T: T = 4 years gives mean SR ~0.77 and ~15 %. Structural: interlayer must be weak enough to fail in ~700 cycles of ~30 K swing but strong enough to survive wind suction (~1-2 kPa) and hail, a narrow window; shed flakes (~100 g/m2 per sheet) are inert mineral litter. Simulation coefficient: T/tau = 1.97 (number of soiling time constants per renewal).
